items.followUp: Describe the cell, tissue and organ levels of organization, giving an example of a tissue.

rubric.why: Identifies an organ as being formed from different tissues and gives the model answer’s example.
rubric.description: Identifies the tissues that form an organ.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an organ is made of different tissues; the example may support the answer.

rubric.why: States that the tissues of an organ work together to perform a function.
rubric.description: Explains the coordinated function of an organ.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the tissues work together to perform a particular function.

rubric.why: Identifies an organ system as organs working together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that several organs work together.

rubric.why: Gives a suitable organ-system example and its function.
rubric.description: Gives an example of an organ system and its function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the digestive system and linking it to digestion, or for another suitable organ-system example with its function.

modelAnswer: At the organ level, different tissues are joined and work together to perform a particular function; for example, the stomach is an organ.
At the organ-system level, several organs work together to perform a major function of the body.
For example, the digestive system consists of organs such as the mouth, stomach and intestines, which work together in digestion.

items.followUp: Name the three main types of plastids and state one feature or function of each.

rubric.why: Defines plastids as organelles found in plant cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying plastids as organelles found in plant cells.

rubric.why: Identifies chloroplasts, their pigment and their role.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking chloroplasts and chlorophyll with photosynthesis.
Award 1 mark for stating that chromoplasts contain coloured pigments.

rubric.why: Identifies leucoplasts as colourless plastids that store food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that leucoplasts are colourless and store food.

rubric.why: Names food materials stored in leucoplasts.
rubric.description: Gives an example of stored food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming at least one stored material, such as starch, oils or proteins.

modelAnswer: Plastids are organelles found in the cytoplasm of plant cells.
Chloroplasts contain the green pigment chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.
Chromoplasts contain coloured pigments and give colour to flowers and fruits.
Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food such as starch, oils and proteins.

items.followUp: How does farming provide food and other useful products?

rubric.why: Identifies crop cultivation as an activity of farming.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that farming involves cultivating or growing crops.

rubric.why: Identifies animal rearing and its useful outcome.
rubric.description: Describes animal farming and its value.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that farming involves rearing animals and provides food or other useful products.

modelAnswer: Farming is the profession of cultivating crops and rearing animals.
It provides food and useful products such as fibre, and may also provide products from livestock.
